mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month signals monetary easing, which lowers discount rates and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises above 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 108.0 signals manufacturing slowdown, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 108.0.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized signals strong economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 is above 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, which may trigger monetary tightening and cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases by at least 0.1 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level below 1200.0 thousand units signals housing market contraction, reducing consumer confidence and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 1200.0.
